::: {#def-exposure-mapping .theorem}
## Exposure mapping

We fix a topological order in which the covariates come in blocks, every entry of $\mathbf{X}_{k-1}$ before every entry of $\mathbf{X}_k$, and in which each graph generator (C.24) sits between two blocks. An exposure mapping is a function

$$
g_{ik}:\mathcal{R}(\mathbf{X}_1)\times\dots\times\mathcal{R}(\mathbf{X}_{k-1})\times\mathcal{R}(\mathbf{X}_{k,<i})\times\mathcal{R}(\boldsymbol{\psi}_1)\times\dots\times\mathcal{R}(\boldsymbol{\psi}_T)\to\mathbb{R}^{m_k}
$$

that selects and transforms the parents of $X_{ki}$ from the variables that precede it, so that its structural equation reads them only through $g_{ik}$:

$$
X_{ki}=f_{X_{ki}}\big(g_{ik}(\mathbf{X}_1,\dots,\mathbf{X}_{k-1},\mathbf{X}_{k,<i},\boldsymbol{\psi}_1,\dots,\boldsymbol{\psi}_T),\,U_{X_{ki}}\big),
$$

where $\mathbf{X}_1,\dots,\mathbf{X}_{k-1}$ are the covariates that precede $X_{ki}$, $\mathbf{X}_{k,<i}$ the elements of its own covariate that precede it, and $\boldsymbol{\psi}_1,\dots,\boldsymbol{\psi}_T$ the graph generators that precede it. $\mathbf{Pa}(X_{ki})$ is the set of arguments on which $g_{ik}$ depends. With a fixed network there are no graph generators, and $g_{ik}$ depends on the network through its definition.
:::
